This widening reflects the difficulty of accounting for all possible outcomes as the time frame lengthens.

Specific risks or unexpected events could push outcomes outside of the stated confidence intervals, especially over the longer horizons. Additionally, unpredictable developments like extreme weather, dramatic supply chain disruptions, or anomalous data behavior could create outcomes well beyond the stated ranges. These risks highlight the importance of monitoring for surprises, especially as uncertainty grows with longer horizons. While the forecast reflects the most likely scenarios and a range of typical variation, it is always possible for real-world events to produce unexpected deviations.
